gitConventions.commitSubject: Spec work: `plan/<id>-<handle>: <task-id> <task title>`, with the same `<id>-<handle>` as the branch, so the commit log reads like the spec's `## Tasks`. Outside a spec: a short imperative, no trailing period and no type prefix — `Regenerate Codex descriptions`.
gitConventions.branchName: `plan/<id>-<handle>`, with the spec id leading; the handle is the kebab-case title and is never parsed back.
gitConventions.prTitle: The spec title verbatim, as `cq specs status` returns it — never a commit subject and never a rewritten summary.
gitConventions.prBody: The spec's `Problem`, `Proposal`, `Impact` and `Validation` sections under headings of those names, the `Tasks` summary with counts, and `Closes #<n>` at the end. Nothing beyond what the spec carries.
gitConventions.mergeSubject: `plan/<id>-<handle>: merge (<strategy>)` for a local merge; a PR merged by GitHub keeps the subject the provider writes.

knowledge.name: Front /docs/
knowledge.description: Work on the OKF bundle in /docs/ — a standard, a glossary entry, the bundle shape, the `cq knowledge` validator and the /quenching:knowledge:* commands. Choose when the deliverable is written knowledge or the structure that holds it.

specs.name: Front de specs
specs.description: Work on the specs front — the /quenching:specs:* commands, `cq specs`, a spec's lifecycle (captured through archive) and the external GitHub Issues and Azure Boards backends. Choose when the deliverable changes how a spec is born, built or closed.

components.name: Front .claude/
components.description: Work on the command surface — the /quenching:components:* commands, `cq components`, command bodies, descriptions, hooks and agents. Choose when the deliverable changes what the surface registers, how a command is routed, or what a description promises.

plugin.name: Plugin (transversal)
plugin.description: Work that crosses more than one front, or is external to the three — release and version lockstep, the marketplace, the README, AGENTS.md, and the shared references under assets/references/align/. Choose when no single front owns the deliverable.

tagCatalog.front:knowledge: Applied automatically by the `knowledge` subject — do not propose on its own.
tagCatalog.front:specs: Applied automatically by the `specs` subject — do not propose on its own.
tagCatalog.front:components: Applied automatically by the `components` subject — do not propose on its own.
tagCatalog.front:plugin: Applied automatically by the `plugin` subject — do not propose on its own.
tagCatalog.breaking: The change breaks an already-installed target repository: a renamed or removed command, a configuration key that stops being read, a frontmatter format that changes. Choose when upgrading the plugin requires human action in the target.
tagCatalog.contract: Changes a written contract that something else cites — a standard in /docs/standards/, a shared reference, the okf-spec. Choose when the text is normative and has citers that must be swept.
tagCatalog.cost: The deliverable is execution cost: tokens a command body reads, tool calls per sweep, reference prose every consumer pays for. Choose when the success measure is a smaller number.
tagCatalog.measured: The spec closes only with evidence collected against a live target — a repository, a board, an API — not just reasoning. Choose when the work requires proving, not arguing.
tagCatalog.regression: Fixes behavior that used to work and stopped working. Choose when an identifiable good earlier state exists, which is the target to restore.

spec.description: Planned behavior change, with problem, proposal and tasks — the normal case in this repository. Choose when the work produces a new deliverable or deliberately changes an existing one.

defect.description: Something declared that does not behave as declared: a command body that contradicts its reference, a tool that exits 0 where it should refuse, a description that promises what the command does not do. Choose when the target is the distance between what is written and what runs.

spike.description: Investigation or measurement whose deliverable is an answer, not code — proving whether a mechanism works, measuring a cost, deciding between two shapes. Choose when success is knowing, not having.

chore.description: Maintenance with no observable behavior change: dedupe, internal rename, tightening prose, moving a file. Choose when a plugin user would notice nothing after the merge.
